scope: Static installed managed CIL and metadata, joined to previously captured native registration assembly; no new runtime experiment, native patch, capacity assumption or target execution.
reaManagedCoverage: REA record matched IMBMission and CompressionMission; nested Integer and AgentCreationResult names were unmatched and independently inspected with Mono.Cecil.
observations: Mission.SpawnAgent calls Mission.CreateAgent; CreateAgent prepares spawn/capsule/animation data then CreateAgentInternal forwards to IMBMission.CreateAgent. Returned AgentCreationResult feeds new managed Agent.

CompressionMission.AgentCompressionInfo is Integer(-1,11); verified two-int constructor treats second arg as numberOfBits and max=min+(1<<bits)-1 => -1..2046. This is wire encoding, not proof of offline allocator capacity.
AgentCreationResult contains direct native field pointers. Pool relocation must account for managed wrappers retaining native addresses.

No literal ldc.i4 2040 or 2047 was found in scanned MountAndBlade/Engine/Core/Library method bodies. 2048 occurrences in the inspected agent construction code are flag checks, not capacity declarations. Scan is bounded to those four assemblies and exact integer literal opcodes.
PrepareImmediately flows to SkinGenerationParams._prepareImmediately then native AddSkinMeshesToAgentEntity. Managed code does not wait or enforce completion.
AgentVisuals.Tick forwards directly to MBAgentVisuals.Tick then native callback. Whether native call waits on face generation, streaming, animation or other jobs remains unknown.

Installed View.AgentVisuals.AddSkinMeshesToEntity does not load forceUseFaceCache argument; faceCacheID is literal zero and final AddSkinMeshes useFaceCache argument is false. Flipping outer Create flag alone cannot enable it via this implementation.
Engine memory statistics APIs are exposed, but no global skeleton or AgentVisual allocation capacity getter was found in the inspected types.
IMBAgentVisuals.BatchLastLodMeshes joins to 0x180047bd0; parent native analysis reports this entry is a return stub. Do not treat its name as active batching support.
inferences: A low-level larger-agent architecture must preserve or virtualize native agent index and field-pointer contracts, not only patch the maximum getter.
Multiplayer index encoding requires a compatible protocol change for agent IDs beyond2046; singleplayer implications require separate native analysis.
Resource-preparation and animation synchronization should be analyzed at their native entries before attributing a rapid-creation slowdown to a fixed pool.
Creation success above2040 should be attributed to the separate parent runtime receipt, not to this static inspection.
unknowns: Allocator capacity and growth behavior behind IMBMission.CreateAgent and native skeleton creation.
Meaning, ownership and range of native visual atlas indices.
Wait conditions and job queues inside AddSkinMeshesToAgentEntity, CheckResources, Tick, TickAnimationsAndForceUpdate.
Whether native Agent field pointers remain stable under any proposed pool growth.
